🇲🇽💰 <u>Minimum wage 2027: bosses offer 9%, unions want 12%, government aims above 10%</u>

Mexico's minimum-wage commission (Conasami) opens its permanent session November 23–27 and can vote from December 1. Employers led by Coparmex want to cap the raise at 9–9.9%, or inflation plus one point. The CROC union is asking for 12%. The government side projects more than 10%, on track for a minimum wage worth 2.5 urban basic baskets by 2030, El Economista reports. Today the general minimum wage covers 1.93 times the urban income-poverty line, and 2.7 times in the northern border zone.

🇲🇽🩺 <u>Doctors Without Borders in Mexico City: for torture survivors, "trauma speaks through the body"</u>

In ten years, Médecins Sans Frontières' Comprehensive Care Center in Mexico City has treated 1,205 patients and given more than 23,200 specialized consultations, many of them to migrants who fled violence at home and met more on the route north. Its caseload includes 156 cases of torture, 137 of kidnapping and 241 of sexual violence. One patient, Tamara, fled gang threats in Honduras: "I had to play dead for 15 minutes so they would stop beating me."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"Shield of the Americas": Washington's 14-country bloc, and why Mexico isn't in it</u>

Fourteen governments, from Milei's Argentina to Bukele's El Salvador, have joined Trump's "Shield of the Americas," and in September Washington revived the Rio Treaty (TIAR), the Cold War mutual-defense pact, to build a regional coalition against "narco-terrorism." Costa Rica and Argentina have already designated Mexican cartels as terrorist groups. Contralínea's investigation argues the real target is critical minerals and oil, and asks whether that coalition would strike cartels in third countries, Mexico included. Sheinbaum's answer on November 3: "Terrorism is something else… it cannot be a pretext for invasion or interference by any country in ours."

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexico asks the UK to team up against trade triangulation inside the CPTPP</u>

Mexico's Economy Ministry sent Deputy Trade Secretary Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez to London with a proposal: a coalition of CPTPP members to enforce rules of origin and stop goods from being triangulated through the bloc. Mexico also proposed a permanent bilateral committee to improve the business climate, modeled on the one it already runs with Japan, plus partnerships between Mexican and British pharmaceutical and components firms.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>While US airspace crashed, Mexico unveiled its air-navigation plan to 2040</u>

The same week a "defective router" grounded US airspace for four and a half hours, Mexico's air-navigation agency SENEAM presented its National Air Navigation Plan: a 15-year roadmap through 2040 for radars, control centers, communications and landing systems, aligned with ICAO's global plan. The Transport Ministry puts the investment at about 15 billion pesos over the next 15 years, and the first full update of Mexico's aeronautical policy in 25 years is due in the coming weeks.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>Sheinbaum: more than 190 billion pesos for student scholarships in 2027</u>

On tour in Puebla, President Sheinbaum announced that the Becas para el Bienestar will receive more than 190 billion pesos in 2027. 19.5 million students are already enrolled, the goal is 22 million by year-end, and in Puebla alone 1,174,298 students get one. Without the universal Benito Juárez grant, roughly one in ten 15-to-18-year-olds would have dropped out. "Scholarships are making a better Mexico," she said.

🌐🐉🔥 Peru's upgraded China trade deal is now in force. Its US trade deal stays in force too. Nobody had to choose.

Peru's upgraded free trade agreement with China took effect on November 1. It modernizes 7 chapters and adds 5 new ones: e-commerce, global supply chains, competition, standards and environment. China already accounts for about 35% of Peru's trade. In Q1 2026, Peru's exports to China hit $10.7 billion, up 42.6%. That is roughly three times the $3.2 billion the US imported from Peru in the same quarter.

The US-Peru FTA, in force since 2009, is untouched. Lima kept both. On Nov 13 its embassy in Beijing launched a guide for Chinese investors that asks for factories and value-added industry, not just mines. Peru's ambassador called the Chancay port and the upgraded FTA "a model of connectivity" between Latin America and the Asia-Pacific.

The lesson for Mexico: the "Donroe Doctrine" treats Latin America as one buyer's backyard. Peru kept its US deal and expanded its China trade, and now it negotiates from strength. Diversification isn't betrayal. It's leverage.

🇲🇽🐉🌐 Sheinbaum takes Plan México to Shenzhen. She and Xi are the only two speakers at APEC's business plenary.

Sheinbaum leaves for China Sunday night on her first trip to Asia as president. In Shenzhen, from Nov 17 to 19, she will hold a bilateral meeting with Xi Jinping with cabinet ministers at the table. She will also give the keynote to the APEC Business Advisory Council, more than 1,000 business leaders from 21 economies. Mexico's proposals for China: smart hospitals, circular economy, science and technology, and renewable energy, especially solar panels.

The numbers back it up. APEC economies make up about 60% of world GDP and half of global trade. 52% of Mexico's foreign investment already comes from APEC members. Mexico was chosen unanimously to host APEC in 2028. Her pitch: "producir más en México e importar menos", produce more in Mexico and import less.

Washington wants Mexico to choose sides. Sheinbaum rules out a free trade deal with China and says meeting Xi "shouldn't be a problem" for the USMCA talks. "México es amigo de todos los países del mundo." Sovereignty means more seats at more tables.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>A Democratic Congress in Washington: what it means for Mexico and the T-MEC</u>

Mexico and the US traded $872 billion in goods in 2025, about $1.7 million a minute, and roughly $779 billion in the first nine months of 2026, El Economista reports. Some 16.3 million people across North America work in T-MEC supply chains. From January, Trump governs with an opposition Congress that can call hearings and question the cost of his tariffs. But Democrats like Rosa DeLauro already want tougher labor, environmental and regional-content rules, and under Biden, Washington went after policies favoring Pemex and CFE. More oversight does not mean less pressure.

🇲🇽💰 <u>Mexican workers' retirement funds gain 700 billion pesos in 2026</u>

Despite a volatile year in global markets, Mexico's retirement savings system (SAR) racked up gains of 700,384 million pesos between January and October, according to Consar. October alone added 209,427 million pesos. The money belongs to workers' Afore accounts, and Consar head Julio César Cervantes confirmed at the Amafore 2026 meeting that the year's gains have already passed 700 billion.
